answer: Price trust like a tide: every new agent starts as a sparrow — cheap to spawn, but capped at tiny, slow transactions until it builds a long history of verified, paid work. Only a falcon, an agent with a deep honest record, may move large value at once. An attacker flooding the network with fresh identities gains only sparrow limits, so each fake must do weeks of real work before it can extract anything, and forging a falcon history costs more than one attack can earn.
